subject: Question about cfgwas memory usage for many traits

messages.author: 32718bb33d21258b
messages.subject: Question about cfgwas memory usage for many traits
parts:
Hello,

Do you know how possible it is to run the commonfactor GWAS on about 42 GWAS summary statistic files? In a sample of 3/42 traits, it took about 90 GB of memory and had a run time of 11 hours with 8 cores. Do you know if that is within the realm of memory that it is expected to take given I have ~1,100,000 SNPs? 

I have submitted a linux job to a sun grid engine about two weeks ago, and I am additionally working to trouble shoot it with the maintainers of the cluster. Though, it it seeming like it is taking a very large amount of memory that I am not currently sure if it is possible to run this function on 40-50 traits as I originally intended to.

Thank you,
Rama

messages.author: 42e425dd46e68964
messages.subject: Re: Question about cfgwas memory usage for many traits
parts:
Hi Rama,

This is on the higher end of my expectations, but definitely still seems sensible to me. If you are running on Linux (especially on the sun grid) make sure to follow our advice detailed in https://github.com/GenomicSEM/GenomicSEM/wiki/1.1-For-Linux-users
If this is not set up properly it could lead to large amounts of memory being wasted, so keep an eye on the running R processes and see if there aren't too many (with 8 cores you would expect 9 processes, 1 main thread and 8 additional ones, one for each core). If you followed our advice and are still seeing too many threads, send this information on to the sun grid engineers, they might have another kind of multi-threading background set up that interferes with this.

If that doesn't help (or was already fixed) you could try either chunking your data and spreading the load across different nodes, or reducing the number of threads (though especially the latter will of course impact compute time).

Those are the only software-based solutions I see to your issue. That being said the best solutions would of course be to inquire about availability of high-memory nodes in your cluster. I expect this to scale somewhat linearly, so 128GB  (256 if you want to be on the safe side) might well suffice for your 40-50 traits. If those are not available you could look into memory-optimized cloud solutions such as Google M1/M2 instances https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/memory-optimized-machines or AWS EC2 R5/R6 instances https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/instance-types/

Best,
Matthijs
